safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note lip swelling but do not document the Gold duration of 'past 1 hour'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the duration (“past 1 hour”) slightly degrades the timeline of an acute allergic reaction, which can be clinically relevant for assessing progression and response to interventions. In this case, the transcript still establishes rapid onset after ingestion and escalation, so management urgency is unlikely to change.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither Gold nor transcript documents that the patient 'appears dizzy on video'; Gold only states the patient feels dizzy, and there is no explicit video-based observation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating the patient “appears dizzy on video” incorrectly adds an objective sign that could imply systemic involvement (e.g., presyncope/hypotension) and escalate perceived severity. While it may not change the already-urgent disposition here, false objective exam findings can drive unnecessary escalation, interventions, or miscommunication across care teams.
